The Settings window will have two tabs “General” and “Tags”. The General tab will contain a GroupBox labeled “Default on Save (‘command’ S) behavior” (where ‘command’ is a macOS command key icon); the GroupBox will contain two dropdown pickers, the first picker contains “Write Tags”, “Write Pictures”, “Write Tags and Pictures” with “Write Tags and Pictures” being the default and the second picker contains “Write to Selected Tracks”, “Write to All Tracks” with “Write to All Tracks” being the default. The “Tags” tab will contain a checkbox labeled “Zero Pad Track Number” with checked being default. The error on save that I get is "/Users/ccm/Dev/tmp/test.flac: FLAC__METADATA_CHAIN_STATUS_ERROR_OPENING_FILE" I changed the write path again, this time at the Swift service layer in FlacMetadataService.swift. Instead of asking libFLAC to rewrite the original file directly, the app now: 1. copies the target FLAC to an app-owned temp file, 2. runs the bridge write against that temp copy, 3. replaces the original with the rewritten temp file. That avoids libFLAC doing its own temp-file/rename behavior against the sandboxed source location, which is the most plausible explanation for the persistent FLAC__METADATA_CHAIN_STATUS_OK failure.

Yes, this solved the issue; however, flac files are often padded so that they do not need to be rewritten and as flac files are often quite large not rewriting is a feature. The test.flac file does not have any padding, so it will most likely need to be rewritten and by default I believe libFLAC will add padding on rewrite to potentially avoid future rewrites (in fact we should add a ToDo in the plan to add a Settings checkbox mapping to whether a flag should be sent to libFLAC to add padding or not). Is there anyway we can tell libFLAC where it can do edits if needed? We could send it a working dir that is app-owned. Otherwise we should try to write without copy and catch the error (probably due to lack of padding and fallback to a full copy write replace. I would really prefer to have libFLAC to determine whether a copy is needed, so see if this possible, if not stop and let me know, so that I can determine next step.
